messages.author: 3ac91e1d284ecac5
messages.subject: Changing axes information plots
parts:
Hi Phil,

I am wondering how to change the axes of the information plots. I would like to have a different minimum and maximum on the y-axis. Also, I have set the range of theta to be -3;5, but my plot shows -2, 0, 2 and 4. Is there any way to change the interval or ticks so that my plot shows -3 and 5 on the x-axis as well?
I am using lattice-extra to make my final plots because I am layering two different information curves in one plot. I have tried different commands that may work with lattice extra but it does not seem to work. Do you have any suggestions?

Thank you!

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Changing axes information plots
parts:
The plots are all objects, so worse case you can edit them directly afterwords:

library(mirt)
mod <- mirt(Science, 1)
plot(mod, xlim=c(-3,5)) # xlim is not reserved, 
plot(mod, xlim=c(-3,5), ylim=c(0,1)) # ylim is reserved and errors

plt <- plot(mod, xlim=c(-3,5)) # ylim is reserved
plt

plt$y.limits
plt$y.limits <- c(3, 20)

plt


Phil

messages.subject: Re: Changing axes information plots
parts:
It should also be noted that using update() is a viable option, which contains better documentation in the update.trellis(). See below for an example, which modifies the ylab of the graphical object:

###

(plt <- itemplot(mod, 1))

# see ?update.trellis
update(plt, ylab = expression(Prob(theta)))
###

Use of the latticeExtra package is often quite useful here too if users are interested in adding additional layers(). 

Phil
